title: Mul 2019 · Full-body illusion and self-location
citation: Mul et al. (2019). Altered bodily self-consciousness and peripersonal space in autism. Autism, 23(8), 2055–2067.
notes: Published study settings are available for inspection. See the source-backed method and remaining execution requirements.

published_method.sequence: The four illusion episodes follow the PPS task. Randomize body versus object crossed with synchronous versus asynchronous stroking, one 120 s episode per condition.
published_method.camera_setup: Custom Unity camera feed to an Oculus Rift CV1. Camera is 230 cm from the visible back or person-sized box. In box conditions the participant stands 100 cm laterally from the box and outside the view. The experimenter stays out of frame.
published_method.stimulation: Stroke the participant's back manually with a stick. For object episodes stroke the box and the participant's back simultaneously at corresponding locations, with two sticks.
published_method.response: After each induction, close eyes, remove HMD, guide the participant 150 cm backward, and record their standing location after they walk to the estimated origin. Follow with seven statements on a seven-level agreement scale, with randomized item order.
published_method.outcome: Calculate self-location drift and score the illusion and control questionnaire items separately. An additional forehead-letter task appears only in the related thesis procedure.

implementation_gaps: Requires controlled live camera and head-mounted display timing with measured end-to-end latency, synchronized manual stroking and a supervised eyes-closed walking protocol.
The original Unity project and frame delivery measurements are unavailable. The software needs an induction, walking and rating sequence and continuous displacement recording.
